title: Chocolate Fondant
subtitle: Warm dark chocolate pudding with a molten centre
excerpt: Individual dark chocolate sponge puddings with a liquid chocolate centre that flows out when the pudding is cut. Dramatic, rich, and surprisingly straightforward to make.

recipe.sourceNotes: The chocolate fondant with a liquid centre (fondant au chocolat or moelleux au chocolat) is generally attributed to French chef Michel Bras, who served a version at his restaurant in Laguiole in 1981. His version involved inserting a pre-frozen ganache disc into the sponge before baking, which gave a reliably liquid centre. The modern restaurant version, as popularised in the 1990s and 2000s, uses an underbaked approach: the batter is the same throughout but the baking time is calibrated so the outside sets while the centre remains liquid. The fondant can be made ahead: pour the batter into the prepared moulds and refrigerate for up to 24 hours, then bake from cold, adding 2 minutes to the baking time. A good-quality dark chocolate (at least 70% cocoa solids) is essential.

recipeTools.notes: Four 180 ml dariole moulds or individual pudding basins.

content.text: Preparing the moulds carefully is essential: butter them generously, then dust with cocoa powder (not flour), tapping out the excess. This allows the fondant to release cleanly when turned out. Oven temperature and baking time are critical and will need testing with your specific oven: at 200 C, most ovens need 10 to 12 minutes for a 180 ml mould. The pudding is ready when the sides are set but the centre resists pressure when lightly pressed. Turn out immediately onto a warm plate and serve at once.

Butter 4 dariole moulds generously and dust with cocoa powder, tapping out the excess. Melt the chocolate and butter together in a bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water, or in a microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring between each. Stir until smooth. Leave to cool slightly.

Whisk the eggs, egg yolks, and sugar together until pale and thick, about 3 minutes with an electric whisk. Fold in the melted chocolate mixture. Sift over the flour and salt and fold in gently until just combined. Divide between the prepared moulds. Refrigerate for at least 20 minutes (or up to 24 hours).

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Place the moulds on a baking tray. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the edges are set but the centre still feels soft and liquid when pressed lightly. Run a knife around the edge of each mould, place a warm plate on top, and invert. Serve immediately with cream or ice cream.
